target_customer: VTubers and avatar content creators, mostly consumers who stream on Twitch and YouTube
problem: VTubing normally needs motion capture hardware and complex software; Hyper lets creators pilot 3D avatars from an iPhone.
business_model: consumer app, creator tools and social avatar platform; monetization not stated

founders.name: Aaron Ng
founders.background_notes: YC page and TechCrunch name him as founder and CEO; neither gives education or employers.

exit.reason: YC marks it Inactive, but the Hyper blog and apps were still live in late 2026 with no shutdown notice.

competitors.name: VTube Studio
competitors.what: iPhone face tracking app that animates Live2D models on PC
competitors.traction_then: Released June 2020, compared with FaceRig by Japanese press

technical_complexity.rationale: Face tracking and avatar rendering on iPhone using ARKit and avatar formats such as VRM was feasible for a small team, with real-time performance and creator tooling as the hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Rival avatar apps and tools could replicate tracking; the platform's social network and creator community were the only potential moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent acquiring or copying Hyper; the product kept shipping through 2026.

market_need_then: VTubing was reaching billions of monthly views on Twitch and YouTube per the YC page, and hardware cost was a barrier for new creators.

branding.domain_note: Used hyper.online rather than an exact .com; no source on how it was obtained.

identity.mascot_or_character: Users' own avatars act as the characters.
identity.voice_and_tone: Creator focused, via a news and guides blog.

branding.brand_signature: Claim to be the number one US VTubing app on iOS, per the YC page.
branding.community_and_virality: A Hyper Discord server listed about 6,200 members on a third party aggregator.

brand_strength.rationale: Active Discord community and a TechCrunch feature, but the name is a generic word and no press about the brand itself was found.

pivots.to: Added Hyper AI, AI driven characters built on OpenAI's GPT, alongside the VTuber tools
pivots.why: Expanding avatar technology to AI assistants and chatbots per TechCrunch.

outcome_analysis: Hyper built an iPhone based VTuber and avatar app, raised a 3.6 million dollar seed led by Two Sigma Ventures in June 2023, and added AI characters. The YC directory marks it Inactive although its blog and apps were still live in late 2026, so the status is unclear and no cause is public. Failure factors stay empty because no source states a failure.
notes: Seed confirmed by TechCrunch and a second outlet (AppMaster, a rewrite). CB Insights lists $4.1M over two rounds, which exceeds the $3.6M seed, so an earlier small round may be missing; not found. Batch conflict: YC directory says Summer 2020 while TechCrunch says Winter 2021 and the YC page says founded 2021. The YC directory shows Inactive while the website shows no shutdown notice; exit type left unknown. The page gives no founder names beyond the YC listing. Competitor VTube Studio dates from June 2020, before the batch; other rivals were undated.
